items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: And the two guys who competed all the time as singers was Billy Eckstine and Bill Kenney, who later on became the lead singer with the Inkspots.

ctx.x: Eckstine came in as a singer. He didn't know how to play a horn at that particular time. So, he was going to Armstrong High School in Washington. And he came in at the Howard Theater in Washington. They used to have an amateur night, I think it was every Wednesday night. I'm not sure of the night.

And the guy who won it would win $50.00. This was a lot of money back then. That was -- man, that was like $5-600.00 now. And the two guys who competed all the time as singers was Billy Eckstine and Bill Kenney, who later on became the lead singer with the Inkspots. And Bill Kenney was from Baltimore. And he became the lead singer.
So, one week Eckstine would win this thing, and another week Kenney -- Bill Kenney would win it.
